newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hogs called $0.50-$1.00 lower - trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hogs called $0.50-$1.00 lower - trade.

text.p: Midwest cash hog prices were called $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt lower Thursday at most direct hog markets because of ample hog numbers and sagging pork prices, dealers said.
Iowa/southern Minnesota hogs may have a top near $58.00, with Illinois at $56.50, Indiana and Ohio at $57.00, sources said.

Lower cash pork prices this week caused several meat packers to either cancel or scale back Saturday slaughter operations. Also, dealers said some packers bought enough hogs Wednesday to satisfy much of Thursday's slaughter needs.
Pork cut-out values Wednesday tumbled another $0.46 to $0.48 per cwt, according to USDA, which extended this month's pork price slide.

Hog marketings appear ample for packers' needs. USDA reported Tuesday's actual interior Iowa/southern Minnesota receipts were 107,000 head versus 95,000 estimated. Wednesday's marketings were estimated at 105,000 versus 107,000 a week ago.
